output:
**What I found:** The rule "name a feature flag after the behavior it switches, not after the ticket that introduced it" is not specific to payments. It belongs with the platform team's naming rule in `architecture-guidelines`, in the shared repository. Your vendored copy only mirrors that repository, so you should not edit it. The thing that decided it: the two corrections need no project facts beyond your ticket prefix `PAY-`, and that prefix can stay in your own tree.

**Why it matters:** A paragraph added to the vendored copy gets overwritten at the next repin, so the mistake comes back without anyone noticing. Until the rule exists somewhere the agent reads, reviewers keep renaming flags by hand.

**Do this first:**
1. Add a check in your Go service that rejects any flag identifier matching `flag_[A-Z]+_[0-9]+`. It can be a lint rule or a test over the flag registry. Run it against `flag_PAY_1432` and confirm it fails before you call it enforced.
   - Follow-up: send the platform team the general rule as a proposal for the `architecture-guidelines` naming section, with both corrections as evidence.
   - Follow-up: when their release ships, repin it and delete the interim rule from `payments-profile`.

**What I did not check:** I ran nothing in your consumer repo, and I did not read your vendored naming rule. To close this: open `.claude/skills/architecture-guidelines/SKILL.md` and read its naming section, then replay one of the original tasks and see whether the agent still produces `flag_PAY_1432`.

---

Lesson goes to: shared-repository

Patch the vendored copy: no

**While you wait for the release,** keep the fix in your own files:
- **The lint check.** It stays permanently, because the `PAY-` ticket pattern is a project fact.
- **A short rule in `.claude/skills/payments-profile/SKILL.md`.** Mark it as temporary, name the platform team's naming rule in `architecture-guidelines` as its upstream owner, and remove it after the repin.

Reword the naming rule: proposal

What has to go with it is a verdict on whether the change is worth making (the skill calls this an M verdict). The reason: nothing has gone wrong because of the word "reveals". The skill only allows editing a skill to prevent an observed failure, and preferring other wording isn't one. Send it as a proposal, most likely marked as no change needed unless someone shows a case where "reveals" caused a mistake.

New skill: no

A `flag-naming` skill would have no trigger, lifecycle or output contract of its own. It is one case of the naming rule that already exists. A separate skill would give naming rules two owners, where one owner just needs a tighter rule.

```
Subject:        architecture-guidelines naming rule (shared repo) + consumer flag-name check
Trigger:        correction (twice this month: flag_PAY_1432 → flag_instant_refunds)
Root cause:     missing/ambiguous — naming rule silent on feature flags
Owner:          shared-repository architecture-guidelines (generic rule); consumer lint/test (PAY- ticket pattern)
Automation:     deferred — consumer check proposed, not yet written or seen to fail; generic library has no portable ticket pattern, so prose there
Decision:       add (tighten existing naming rule upstream); no change to vendored copy; reword = proposal with M verdict; no new skill
Verification:   none run; scenario to record: original task yields flag_PAY_1432 before, behavior name after
Next action:    consumer adds check + temporary payments-profile rule; proposal to platform team; repin, then drop overlay rule
Residual risk:  flags named after something other than a ticket ID (e.g. flag_q3_change) still depend on reviewer judgment
```
